patient_information: A 24-year-old man of Turkish origin, a German resident, who visits his family in rural eastern Turkey (Anatolia) every year for about 6 weeks.
chief_complaint: Right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting.
history_of_present_illness: Three years prior, the patient presented with right upper quadrant pain, revealing two calcified cystic liver lesions via ultrasound and CT scan, diagnosed as cystic echinococcosis (CE) with positive serology for Echinococcus granulosus; anthelmintic treatment was not considered, and surgical treatment was refused, with cysts monitored by ultrasound for signs of spontaneous involution.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Visits family in rural eastern Turkey (Anatolia) every year for about 6 weeks, which is a hyperendemic region for CE.
physical_exam: Fair general condition with scleral jaundice, right upper quadrant and epigastric tenderness, but no guarding.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count is normal. AST 145 U/L (>35), ALT 454 U/L (>35), GGT 394 U/L (>55), ALP 402 U/L (38-126), Total bilirubin 120 µmol/L (<19.0), ESR 17/40 mm/h (≤10/20), CRP 49 mg/L (<5). Ultrasound at prior diagnosis showed two cystic lesions with partially calcified walls (Fig. 50.1A and B), and a CT scan showed both cyst walls calcified (Fig. 50.2).
differential_diagnosis: Congenital simple hepatic cyst, pseudocysts (necrotic cavity) in alveolar echinococcosis (E. multilocularis), bacterial or amoebic abscesses, tuberculoma, benign and malignant liver tumours or metastases.
management_and_clinical_course: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography (ERC) revealed biliary obstruction due to a cystobiliary fistula; CE cyst content was removed, bile flow restored, and cholangitis treated with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. After inflammation settled, partial cystectomy was performed on both cysts. The patient has been followed up for 9 years post-surgery with no recurrence and is considered cured.
final_diagnosis: Cystic Echinococcosis with cystobiliary fistula and bacterial cholangitis.

images.caption: Ultrasound scan of the liver at diagnosis 3 years before current presentation reveals two cystic lesions. One lesion is located in the right liver lobe (7 x 6cm). Cyst content shows a solid cyst matrix containing multiple smaller cysts (A). The cyst wall is partially calcified (WHO classification CE3b).

Second cystic lesion in the left liver lobe (5 x 4 cm). The cyst wall is up to 4 mm thick with partial calcification. Cyst content is liquid; there is a double line sign, a feature of WHO CE1, and hydatid sand.
Computed tomography of the same patient. Both cyst walls show calcification.
